# Participant Demographics

This section focuses on the demographics of the survey participants. I will 
use the data frame provided earlier to analyze and report on the demographics of 
survey participants. No further cleaning of the data frame occurs in this 
section.

```{r}
#| label: set-demog-Setup
#| include: false
#| echo: false

library('tidyverse')
library('ggthemes')

source("_graph_standards_bar.R")

main_df <- readRDS("main_df.rds")
```

## Participant Age Grouping Demographics

The age demographics of participants is fairly well spread out with most of the 
people reporting an age of 45-54 years old. This is a bell curve that is 
weighted a bit more towards the 65+ over the 18-24 year old participants. As 
previously indicated, all participants reporting ages under 18 or skipped 
reporting their age were removed from this research analysis.

```{r}
#| label: fig-demog-AgeChart
#| fig-cap: "Survey Participants by Age Group"
#| fig-height: 4

graph_bar_chart(main_df, 
                'Age', 
                'Age Grouping', 
                'Participant Count')
```

## Participant Gender Demographics

Male participants represent approximately 76% of respondents with Female 
participants at roughly 24%. One respondent did not report gender and is 
excluded from gender-based comparisons. This gender skew is consistent with the 
broader gender imbalance in the IT industry and should be considered when 
interpreting results.

NEED BETTER STATEMENT AND CITATION.
Gender imbalance is well documented through research. The WorldBank 2025 report 
on Digital Progress and Trends notes that women only make up 24 percent of 
Information and Communication Technology professionals world-wide.

<https://openknowledge.worldbank.org/server/api/core/bitstreams/99474f35-6a0c-48c3-9104-7b693e04313e/content>


```{r}
#| label: fig-demog-GenderChart
#| fig-cap: "Survey Participants By Gender"
#| fig-height: 3

graph_bar_chart(main_df,
                'Gender',
                'Gender',
                'Participant Count')
```

The table below restricts the comparison to respondents who identified as
Male or Female, excluding those who did not report a gender or selected
"Prefer not to say."

```{r}
#| label: tbl-demog-GenderMaleFemale
#| tbl-cap: Male vs. Female Participants (Excluding NA and Prefer Not to Say)

main_df |>
  filter(Gender %in% c("Male", "Female")) |>
  count(Gender, name = "n") |>
  mutate(Percent = paste0(round(n / sum(n) * 100, 1), "%")) |>
  knitr::kable(col.names = c("Gender", "Count", "Percent"),
               align = c("l", "r", "r"))
```

## Participant Country Demographics

The United States accounts for the large majority of respondents. The remaining
participants represent eight other countries, none exceeding 5% of the sample
individually. Given this concentration, country of residence is not examined as
an independent variable in the analysis.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-demog-CountryTable
#| tbl-cap: Participants By Country

main_df |>
  mutate(Country = recode(Country,
    "United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland" = "United Kingdom"
  )) |>
  count(Country, name = "n") |>
  mutate(
    Country = tidyr::replace_na(as.character(Country), "Not Reported"),
    Percent = paste0(round(n / nrow(main_df) * 100, 1), "%")
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(n)) |>
  knitr::kable(col.names = c("Country", "Count", "Percent"),
               align = c("l", "r", "r"))
```

## Participant Education Level Demographics

This analysis shows a fairly diverse education level for the participants. 
Bachelor's (or equivalent) and Graduate Degree holders representing the 
majority of survey participants with almost 80% of respondents.

```{r}
#| label: fig-demog-EducationChart
#| fig-cap: "Survey Participants By Education Level"
#| fig-height: 5
#| out-width: "100%"

graph_bar_chart(main_df, 
                'Education', 
                'Education Level', 
                'Participant Count')
```

## Participant IT Field Demographics

Participants represent a wide range of IT specializations. Software Development 
is the most common field at 22% of respondents, followed by Cloud Infrastructure 
& DevOps (11%), Database Management & ERP (9%), and Systems & Network 
Administration (9%). Data & Analytics and IT Support & Help Desk each account 
for roughly 7-8%. The remaining participants are distributed across eight other 
specializations.

```{r}
#| label: fig-demog-ITFieldChart
#| fig-height: 8
#| fig-cap: "Survey Participants By IT Field"
#| out-width: "100%"

graph_bar_chart(main_df, 
                'IT_Field', 
                'IT Field', 
                'Participant Count')
```

## Participant IT Industry Demographics

The sample is heavily concentrated in two industries. Healthcare & Life Science 
account for 51% of respondents. Information Technology accounts for an 
additional 20%. The remaining 29% are distributed across twelve other 
industries, with Education and Government & Public Sector each representing 
about 4%. The concentration in Healthcare & Life Science likely reflects the 
distribution channels I used to recruit participants.

```{r}
#| label: fig-demog-ITIndustryChart
#| fig-cap: "Survey Participants By IT Industry"
#| fig-height: 7
#| out-width: "100%"

graph_bar_chart(main_df, 
                'IT_Industry', 
                'IT Industry', 
                'Participant Count')
```

## Conclusion

This section highlights the demographics of the survey participants. Notable
results from this section include:

* Age Groups are represented with a bell curve weighted more towards the older
groups than younger groups.
* Gender imbalance reflects the IT Industry as a whole.
* The United States represents the largest number of survey takers.
* Education has most respondents reporting Bachelor or Graduate degrees.
* A diverse representation from different IT Fields are represented.
* The IT Industry is heavily represented by Healthcare and Life Science jobs.
